title: Why Leaves Change Color: The Green Secret

scenes.title: THE GREEN LEAF
scenes.caption: Chlorophyll reflects green light and helps capture sunlight.
scenes.narration: Inside each leaf, chlorophyll helps capture sunlight and power photosynthesis. That green pigment is why most leaves look green through spring and summer.

scenes.title: SUNLIGHT POWERS THE LEAF
scenes.caption: Chlorophyll helps plants turn light into energy.
scenes.narration: Chlorophyll absorbs much of the red and blue light. The energy helps the plant make sugars that support growth.

scenes.title: A TINY CELL FACTORY
scenes.caption: Leaf cells contain many chloroplasts.
scenes.narration: Inside leaf cells are chloroplasts, tiny structures where photosynthesis takes place. They are packed with the green pigment chlorophyll.

scenes.title: THE GREEN ENGINE
scenes.caption: Chlorophyll is continually made and replaced.
scenes.narration: During the growing season, plants keep making chlorophyll. This steady supply masks other pigments already present in the leaf.

scenes.title: SUNLIGHT AND TEMPERATURE
scenes.caption: Long bright days support active growth.
scenes.narration: Warm days and plenty of light help many trees maintain their green leaves and keep photosynthesis running.

scenes.title: MORE THAN ONE COLOR
scenes.caption: Green is only part of the story.
scenes.narration: A leaf contains several pigments. Green chlorophyll dominates for much of the year, but other colors are waiting underneath.
